headline: US Senator Bernie Sanders rejected OpenAI chief executive Sam Altman's suggestion that society may have to accept severe AI cyber incidents in exchange for open models.
score_reason: Lowered from 6: Sanders posted on Monday 12 October, before the window; the exchange is a political reply, not a new policy step.
importance_line: The exchange shows the open-model security debate moving into politics, where Sanders and Representative Greg Casar have a bill to ban superintelligence while the Trump administration and House Speaker Mike Johnson favour lighter rules, but the bill has not passed.
summary: Benzinga reports, as carried by Yahoo, that Bernie Sanders, independent US senator from Vermont, wrote on X "No, Mr. Altman. We won't accept a severe AI cyberattack in exchange for 'liberty,'" and called for a pause on advanced AI and a permanent ban on artificial superintelligence. He was answering Altman's remark on Politico's Decoded podcast last week that society may "have to just accept some fairly severe cyber incidents from open models, in exchange for the liberty that comes with that."
notes: Reply story: Sanders answers Altman's Politico Decoded remarks made the week before (exact date not given). Page text is Benzinga's (disclosure line names Benzinga and Yahoo Finance); url is the Yahoo page where it was read.
